authorities.name: Children and Families Act 2014, s.42
authorities.date_note: Date this section came into force. The text verified this session is the current in-force version.
authorities.proposition: Where a local authority maintains an Education, Health and Care (EHC) plan for a child or young person, it must secure the specified special educational provision (s.42(1)-(2)); if the plan specifies health care provision, the responsible commissioning body must arrange that provision (s.42(3)).
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly this session.

authorities.name: R (BA) v Nottinghamshire County Council
authorities.court: High Court (Queen's Bench Division, Administrative Court)
authorities.judge_or_panel: HHJ Coe QC (Deputy High Court Judge)
authorities.proposition: Section 42 imposes an absolute and non-delegable duty on local authorities to secure the special educational provision specified in an EHC plan, following R (N) v North Tyneside Borough Council [2010] EWCA Civ 135 (not independently verified in this file). There is no 'best endeavours' defence - the authority cannot discharge the duty merely by showing it tried its best, for example by relying on a school or third party. If circumstances change, the plan itself must be revised through the statutory machinery; while it stands, the authority must implement it.
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly from Find Case Law this session, independently re-fetched and re-confirmed a second time - both fetches word-for-word consistent on paragraph 27's absolute-duty holding. Cross-checked against IPSEA's case summary (which also notes this reasoning has since been applied in King v Westmorland and Furness Council [2024] and HXN v London Borough of Redbridge [2024] EWHC 443 (Admin), neither independently verified here) and a Lexology/Birkett Long commentary. High Court decision, recorded as PERSUASIVE authority weight.

edges.verified_via: R (BA) v Nottinghamshire CC [2021] EWHC 1348 (Admin), para 27, fetched directly from Find Case Law and independently re-confirmed: construes s.42 as an absolute, non-delegable duty with no best-endeavours defence.

what_this_is_not: Two verified nodes covering the absolute nature of the s.42 duty. Does not cover the EHC needs assessment/plan process itself, school exclusion appeal rights, SEND Tribunal procedure, or any other Education Law subject - all remain unbuilt.
